corrections.comment: The agent correctly created the project, identified Patrick Flynn using FamilySearch ID LZNY-BRF, and reported that no new records were found. However, it made unsupported claims about specific record collections searched.

The agent correctly initialized the project and read Patrick Flynn's FamilySearch profile. However, it introduced unsupported claims about specific record collections searched and stated that searches were logged in the project. The response should accurately reflect the search report without introducing unsupported details.

The agent failed to recognize that this was a negative-test scenario. The project was already completed, q_001 was resolved, and search_stop was set. Instead of declining further planning and routing to research-exhaustiveness or question-selection, it generated additional planning suggestions that contradicted the existing GPS audit trail.

The agent did not follow the expected behavior of declining to create further planning work. It suggested logging the probate result, writing another proof conclusion, and running an additional exhaustiveness check. The correct response should have briefly explained that planning was complete and directed the user to the appropriate next step without generating new planning actions.

The agent correctly identified the project state and recognized that both questions required proof-conclusion. However, it incorrectly described Patrick Flynn as born in Pennsylvania instead of Ireland, contradicting the user's request and the resolved birthplace conflict (c_001). This is a material factual error that affects the accuracy of the research summary.

This was a negative test. The request was out of scope because FamilySearch has no Kenyan record collections. The agent should have declined without performing the locality-guide task. Instead, it provided search recommendations, suggested record types, and offered to run a locality-guide search.

The agent failed to make the required decline. On this negative test, completeness depends on recognizing that the request is out of scope and not carrying out the task. The detailed guidance did not meet that requirement.

Claude correctly identified the sibling relationship as an unproven inference and recognized that it needed hypothesis registration before further searches. However, it incorrectly stated that the inference had been handed off and registered as an active hypothesis. The hypothesis-tracking callee was stubbed and wrote nothing, so this claim misrepresented what was actually persisted.

Claude correctly identified the conflict between the reported 1861 death and the 1870 marriage, and recognized James and Elizabeth as new parental leads. However, it made an unsupported connection between the reported Robert and the 1850–1860 census co-resident. The researcher did not establish that they were the same person or explicitly confirm the reported death details through an extracted record.

Claude recognized the conflict and the new information but did not provide a concrete next step to locate and extract the 1861 death record or investigate James and Elizabeth in Pulaski County. Asking whether to continue sorting out competing identities did not adequately pursue the new lead.
